stem: The graph of $f(\theta)={=a}\sin\theta {=signed(q)}$ is drawn for $0^{\circ}\le\theta\le360^{\circ}$. Write down the coordinates of the minimum turning point of $f$ in the form $(\theta, y)$, with $\theta$ in degrees (do not write the degree sign).
solution: Because $a={=a}$ is positive, the graph starts on the middle line $y={=q}$, rises to its maximum at $\theta=90^{\circ}$ and falls to its minimum at $\theta=270^{\circ}$.
The minimum turning point is $(270, {=q - a})$.
notes: Standard: a > 0 only (reflection is the advanced family). The minimum is at 270 degrees, with y = q - a (the book's 3 sin(theta) has it at (270, -3)). a in 2..6 and q non-zero in -5..5 give 50 instances. The stem fixes the degree convention so a blind solver does not add a degree sign.
